newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ST CAPITAL MAKES PROVISION FOR THAI ASSETS.
newsitem.headline: ST CAPITAL MAKES PROVISION FOR THAI ASSETS.

text.p: ST Capital Ltd said on Thursday that a significant drop in first half profit at the company level was due largely to provision made for potential diminution in value of its Thai baht earning assets.

"With the provision made in the first half, the group would have sufficient reserves to bear the full impact of the foreign exchange loss arising from the Thai baht float at the current US$/Thai baht exchange rate," it said in statement reviewing the first half results.
The higher Singapore dollar interest rate in the first half also contributed to the decline in profits as interest spreads narrowed and interest rate swap income declined.
It said earning assets grew five percent in the first half to S$1.06 billion compared with the year-end 1996 position.
"The slow growth is a reflection of the difficult operating environment and limited lending opportunities, particularly in the Singapore market."
ST Capital said the second half was expected to be more difficult as Southeast Asian countries adjusted to the progressive weakening of their currencies and higher interest rates.
"Credit risk has increased as foreign exchange losses begin to plague companies in the region, which are accustomed to borrowing foreign currencies on an unhedged basis."
The company said it would take a cautious approach to regional business expansion and expected the second half performance to be comparable to the first six months.
ST Capital shares have been sold down in recent weeks on speculation over its Thai exposure. It closed unchanged at S$1.27 on Thursday.
